title: Billing reconciliation pipeline + tamper-evident audit trails for metering
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: Our billing pipeline must provide provable, tamper-evident records for metered usage so finance and auditors can validate charges. Current gaps: (1) intermediate aggregation steps do not publish immutable manifests; (2) reconciliation run results are not cryptographically verifiable and have no retention guarantees aligned with SOC2/finance; (3) access to raw usage logs is broad and not tightly scoped by role; (4) there is no automated drift detection between usage meters and billed line items. Goal: deliver an end-to-end solution that (a) emits append-only, signed manifests for each billing window, (b) runs automated reconciliations with alerting on divergence beyond tolerance, (c) enforces least-privilege access to raw logs and manifests, and (d) produces a SOC-friendly evidence package (retention, integrity proofs, access logs) for auditors.
acceptance_criteria:
1) For each billing window, a manifest file (JSONL summary) is written to the immutable store with an HMAC signature using a KMS-protected key; manifests include source IDs, aggregation version, checksum of underlying shard files, and sequence number.
2) Reconciliation job runs nightly and produces a delta report; deltas > 0.1% or > $100 trigger high-priority alert and create a ticket automatically.
3) Reconciler exposes metrics: drift_ratio, last_success_ts, files_verified, signatures_verified.
4) Raw usage and manifest access is logged to an audit trail stored for 7 years; RBAC rules limit S3/DB access to "billing_read" and "billing_admin" roles only.
5) Provide a playbook and pre-assembled auditor evidence bundle containing: signed manifests, reconciliation runs, key rotation history, access audit logs, and PR/announcements for any corrections.
6) Unit and integration tests validate signature verification, compromised-key rotation handling, and forced-drift simulation.
7) Design reviewed and approved by Security and Finance; security_review_required flagged true and security review completed in the loop.
comments: 2025-01-12 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff with Finance and Security. Agreed scope: manifests + reconciler + RBAC audit logs. Finance requires retention >= 6 years; legal recommends 7 years for invoicing evidence.

2025-01-18 - Marcus Nguyen: PoC implemented for signed manifest generation. Using KMS HMAC with key alias alias/billing-manifests. Writing to S3 with object lock in Governance mode for the initial prototype. Performance: signing adds ~4ms per manifest generation (acceptable).
2025-01-22 - Security (review): Feedback - switch from HMAC to asymmetric signing for non-repudiation and easier key rotation auditability. Also require separate key for test/preview environments.

2025-01-25 - Marcus Nguyen: Updated PoC to use RSA signing via KMS asymmetric keys. Adjusted manifest schema to include signer_key_id and key_version. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4987

2025-01-28 - Finance (review): Confirmed acceptance criteria for tolerances and requested additional fields in the manifest: customer_contract_id and pricing_tier at aggregation time for cross-checking against billing catalog.

2025-01-30 - Marcus Nguyen: Nightly reconciler implemented, compares aggregator output to billed ledger. Added metrics and prometheus exporter. Initial run flagged 0.08% drift and created internal ticket for investigation.
2025-02-01 - QA: Added integration tests to simulate shard loss and verify reconciler detects >0.1% drift and raises alert. Tests pass locally. Preparing e2e in staging.

2025-02-02 - Marcus Nguyen: Security review scheduled for 2025-02-04. Next steps: finalize RBAC policy, complete PR review, and deploy to staging in audit-only mode (no customer-facing adjustments) before full rollout.
implementation_notes:
Implementation decisions to date: asymmetric KMS keys for manifest signing, store manifests in write-once S3 with object lock + separate index in DynamoDB for fast lookups, reconciler runs as serverless job with checkpointing, reconciler writes signed delta reports. We will instrument verification on read paths (billing UI + exports) to validate signatures before allowing download. Key rotation: generate new KMS key quarterly, record rotation events in manifest metadata, and retain old public keys for verification. Forensics: maintain a signed chain-of-custody file per month.
Open questions: archival compression strategy vs verification cost, retention beyond 7 years for global legal needs, and integration of signed manifests into customer invoices for high-risk customers.
qa_plan: Create synthetic traffic to exercise edge-case metering (very short-lived sessions, high-concurrency bursts), run reconciler in staging, inject simulated shard replays and missing files to validate alerts. Audit team to run verification scripts against staging bundle. Capture test evidence artifacts and add to evidence bundle for SOC audit.
